title: Van Gogh
examples: What kind of colors did Van Gogh like to use?
Can you tell me more about his time in the asylum?
How did his paintings capture movement?

explain.say: Van Gogh used a very noticeable technique with his paint.
This thick paint style is called impasto, and it adds texture to the art.
One famous painting showing this technique is Starry Night.
He also painted many beautiful pictures of sunflowers.
Van Gogh's life was quite difficult, involving many changes.
In real life, you can see this technique on some sculptures.

faq.q: What does impasto mean in art?
faq.a: Impasto is a technique where paint is laid on thickly so that the brushstrokes are visible. It gives the painting a very three-dimensional texture.
asks: What is the name for thick paint?
How do you make paint look bumpy?

faq.q: Why are his paintings so emotional?
faq.a: Van Gogh used color and visible strokes to express strong feelings, which is a key part of Post-Impressionism. The art reflects his inner emotional state.
asks: Does his art show his feelings?
What is the mood of his paintings?

faq.q: What is the significance of Starry Night?
faq.a: Starry Night is famous for its swirling, visible brushstrokes and dramatic use of color, capturing a sense of energy in the night sky.
asks: Why is Starry Night so popular?
What makes the sky look like that?

faq.a: Yes, Van Gogh painted many series of sunflowers. These flowers are known for their bright, vibrant yellow color.
asks: What flowers did he paint a lot?

faq.q: What art movement is he associated with?
faq.a: He is strongly associated with Post-Impressionism. This movement came after Impressionism and focused more on emotion than just light.
asks: What group of artists was he in?
Is he Impressionist or something else?

facts: Van Gogh used visible, thick paint strokes, a technique called impasto.
Starry Night is famous for its dramatic, swirling depiction of the night sky.
He painted several series of bright yellow sunflowers.
His life was marked by periods of intense creativity and personal struggle.

quiz.say: The technique of applying paint thickly to show texture is called:
quiz.why: Impasto is the specific art term for painting with visible, thick layers of paint.

wrong.0: Sfumato is a technique creating soft, smoky transitions between colors.
wrong.1: Blending is a general term, but impasto describes the physical thickness of the paint.
wrong.3: Glazing means applying thin, transparent layers of paint over a dry surface.

quiz.say: Which painting is famous for its swirling, energetic night sky?
quiz.why: Starry Night is the iconic piece that displays his energetic use of thick paint.

wrong.1: Sunflowers are known for their bright color, not primarily the swirling sky.
wrong.2: While he painted portraits, Starry Night is the piece defining his sky work.
wrong.3: Wheat Field shows color, but Starry Night captures the specific cosmic energy.

quiz.say: If an artist wants the paint texture to be very obvious, they should use:
quiz.why: Using thick paint directly creates the physical texture that defines impasto.

wrong.0: Watery paint thins the color and makes the texture disappear.
wrong.1: A wash is very dilute and will not build up visible paint layers.
wrong.2: Airbrushing creates a smooth, uniform mist, the opposite of thick paint.
